purpose: Chapter 4: distinguish delivery, startup and running ramp rate
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: full-width teaching illustration for a technical data-center course.
Primary request: Explain why three meanings of "fast" in gas-fired power are different: acquiring/building a power plant, restarting a warm available plant, and adjusting the output of an already running plant. Make one coherent left-to-right visual narrative using the same stylized combined-cycle plant in three successive states, not a dashboard of disconnected facts.
Style: exceptionally polished editorial engineering illustration, crisp architectural isometric shapes, warm ivory background, deep teal machinery, restrained amber heat accents, fine clean outlines. Educational conceptual illustration, not a photograph or an asserted OEM layout.
Composition: wide landscape 16:9. Three spacious equally sized scenes connected along one thin continuous horizontal time ribbon. First scene: construction crane installing a closed gas-turbine enclosure next to a separate steam-system building, with a large calendar icon. Second scene: the completed plant warming and starting, with a clock icon and subtle amber heat held within the machinery (no flames outside); no cranes. Third scene: same completed plant operating, with one simple rising electrical-output line and a sloped-arrow icon showing adjustment; no new construction.
Text verbatim, large and sharply readable: over the first scene "DELIVERY"; over second "STARTUP"; over third "RAMPING". Under scenes respectively: "Equipment + construction", "Stopped → generating", "Changing running output". No other text, numbers, statistics or title.
Accuracy constraints: All scenes depict a gas-turbine plant with an additional distinct steam-system building. Do not draw gas turning into steam, detailed internal turbine anatomy, imaginary exposed electrical wiring, smoke pollution, or utility transmission diagrams. Keep the output line conceptual with no numerical axes; it is not measured data.
Avoid: crowded labels, tiny captions, logos, watermarks, charts with invented data, gradients behind text, decorative panels. Leave generous margins and strong separation between all text and machinery.
limitations: Conceptual plant illustration, not an OEM equipment arrangement. Curve is qualitative, with no measured data or numerical axes. Catalog ratings are supported separately in the reader.
review: Reviewed generated output for exact labels, text separation and conceptual sequence.
